- push every opening bracket;

## Solution

**Characterization.** Let $M = 2^p q^2$ with $p,q\ge 1$. Write $q = 2^b r$ with $r$ odd. Then
$$M = 2^{p+2b} r^2 .$$
So the odd part of $M$ is $r^2$ (a perfect square) and $v_2(M) = p+2b \ge 1$.

Conversely, if $M = 2^a s^2$ with $s$ odd and $a\ge 1$, take $p=a\ge1$, $q=s\ge1$ — it's splendid.

**So:** $M$ is splendid $\iff$ $M$ is even and its odd part is a perfect square, i.e. $M = 2^a s^2$ with $a\ge 1$, $s$ odd. This representation is unique ($a=v_2(M)$), so there's no double counting.

**Counting.** For each $a = 1,2,\dots,\lfloor\log_2 K\rfloor$:
$$2^a s^2 \le K \iff s^2 \le \lfloor K/2^a\rfloor \iff s \le t_a := \left\lfloor\sqrt{\lfloor K/2^a\rfloor}\right\rfloor$$
The number of odd $s$ in $[1,t_a]$ is $\lfloor (t_a+1)/2\rfloor$. Sum over $a$.

## Solution Idea

**Step 1 — What is $g(p,q)$?**

An operation erases all copies of $s,s+1,\dots,t$, and requires every one of those integers to be present. So a chosen range can never jump over a value that is absent from the board. Hence each operation stays inside one *maximal run of consecutive integers* of the distinct value set, and a whole maximal run can be erased in a single operation. Erasing never creates new values, so

$$g(p,q)=\#\{\text{distinct values in }B_p..B_q\}-\#\{v:\ v\text{ and }v+1\text{ both occur in }B_p..B_q\}.$$

**Step 2 — Sum of distinct counts over all subarrays**

Classic: with `last[B_i]` = previous position of the same value (0 if none),

$$\sum_{p\le q}\#\text{distinct} = \sum_{i=1}^{M}(i-\text{prev}_i)\cdot(M-i+1).$$

**Step 3 — For each $v$, count subarrays containing both $v$ and $v+1$**

For a fixed right end $q$, the valid left ends are $p\le\min(\text{last}_v(q),\text{last}_{v+1}(q))$, so the count is
$\sum_q \min(\text{last}_v(q),\text{last}_{v+1}(q))$.

This quantity only changes at positions where $v$ or $v+1$ occurs, so we can compute it by **merging the two occurrence lists**, in $O(|P_v|+|P_{v+1}|)$ time. Summed over all $v$ this is $O(M)$ total, since each occurrence list is used twice.
